title: System Protocol 1: Classes and Objects
lessonSummary: Great! You build a class and create objects with attributes.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a class, an object, two attributes.
tasks.codeTemplate:
class Robot:
    pass

robot = Robot()
robot.name = "Nova"
robot.level = 1
print(robot.name, robot.level)

tasks.instruction: Create a class Robot with `pass`. Create an object robot, set `name` to Nova and `level` to 3 and print exactly Nova has Level 3 with an f-string.
tasks.codeTemplate: # 🎯 Your solution here:

tasks.instruction: The empty class Robot is given. Create two objects robot (Nova, level 1) and robot2 (Orbit, level 1). Raise the level to 5 only for robot and print Nova: 5 and Orbit: 1 on two lines.

title: System Protocol 2: The Constructor __init__
lessonSummary: Nice! Your constructor sets the starting values for every new object.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a constructor with a default value.
tasks.codeTemplate:
class Robot:
    def __init__(self, name, level=1):
        self.name = name
        self.level = level

a = Robot("Nova")
b = Robot("Orbit", 5)
print(a.name, a.level)
print(b.name, b.level)

tasks.instruction: Write a class Robot with `__init__(self, name, level=1, energy=100)` that stores all three values. Create robot = Robot("Nova", 4) and print exactly Nova 4 100 with an f-string (name, level, energy).
tasks.codeTemplate: # 🎯 Your solution here:

tasks.instruction: The class Robot with `__init__(self, name, level=1)` is given. Create an object Zeta without a level and an object Orbit with level 7 and print Zeta: Level 1 and Orbit: Level 7 on two lines.

title: System Protocol 3: Methods and self
lessonSummary: Well done! Your objects can now do something.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a method with self.
Write a class Robot with `__init__(self, name, level)` and the method `introduce(self)` that prints I am Nova, Level 2. (name and level from `self`). Create Robot("Nova", 2) and call the method.
tasks.codeTemplate: # 🎯 Your solution here:

tasks.instruction: The class Robot with the method `introduce()` is given. Create Robot("Orbit", 4) and Robot("Zeta", 6) and call `introduce()` on both.

validation.expected:
I am Orbit, Level 4.
I am Zeta, Level 6.

tasks.instruction: Write a class Robot with `__init__(self, name)` (level starts at 1) and the method `upgrade(self)` that raises the level by 1 and prints Nova gets an upgrade: Level 3. Create Robot("Nova") and call `upgrade()` twice.
tasks.codeTemplate: # 🎯 Your solution here:

title: System Protocol 4: Methods with Parameters and return
lessonSummary: Super! Your methods take values and return results.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a method with a parameter and one with return.
The class Robot is given (`work(kosten)` lowers the energy, it never drops below 0). Create Robot("Nova"), call `work(40)` and `work(70)` and print exactly Energy: 0.

Write a class Robot with `__init__(self, name, energy)` and a method `is_tired(self)` that returns **True** if the energy is below 20 (otherwise False). Print the results for Robot("Nova", 10) and Robot("Orbit", 80) (two lines).
tasks.codeTemplate: # 🎯 Your solution here:

tasks.instruction: The class Robot is given (`recharge(menge)` raises the energy, at most up to 100). Create Robot("Nova", energy=20), call `recharge(50)` twice and print exactly Energy: 100.

title: System Protocol 5: Changing the State
lessonSummary: Strong! Your objects remember their state.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a counter inside the object.
The class Robot is given. Create Robot("Nova"), call `work(30)`, then `recharge(50)` (at most 100!) and then `work(20)`. Print exactly Energy: 80.
Write a class Robot with `__init__(self, name)` (attribute `wins` starts at 0) and the method `win(self)` that raises `wins` by 1. Call it three times and print exactly Wins: 3.
tasks.codeTemplate: # 🎯 Your solution here:

tasks.instruction: The class Robot is given. Create Robot("Nova"), call `upgrade()` three times and then print exactly Level: 4.

title: System Protocol 6: Objects in Lists
lessonSummary: Nice! You manage whole groups of objects.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: looping over objects in a list.
The class Robot is given. Create the list `gruppe` with Robot("Nova", 3), Robot("Orbit", 8) and Robot("Zeta", 5) and print every name on its own line with a `for` loop.
The class Robot and the list `gruppe` (levels 3, 8, 5) are given. Find the object with the highest level with a loop and print exactly Strongest: Orbit.
The class Robot and the list `gruppe` (levels 3, 8, 5) are given. Build the list `starke` of all names with level 5 or more with a list comprehension and print it with `print(starke)`.

title: System Protocol 7: Passing Objects to Functions
lessonSummary: Well done! You now know how objects and functions work together.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: two names for one object.
tasks.codeTemplate:
class Robot:
    def __init__(self, name, level):
        self.name = name
        self.level = level

a = Robot("Nova", 1)
b = a
b.level = 10
print(a.level)

tasks.instruction: The class Robot is given. Write a function `stronger(a, b)` that returns the object with the higher level. Compare Robot("Nova", 4) and Robot("Orbit", 9) and print exactly Winner: Orbit.
The class Robot and the object `robot = Robot("Nova")` are given. Give the object a second name `zweiter`, set the level to 9 through `zweiter` and print exactly Nova: Level 9 through `robot`.

The class Robot and the list `gruppe` (levels 3, 8, 5) are given. Write a function `train_all(gruppe)` that does `level += 1` for everyone (no return). Call it and print exactly Sum: 19 (sum of all levels).

title: Extra Challenge 4: The Great Guild
lessonSummary: Done: classes work together with everything you have learned!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – functions and lists: the class Robot is given. Write `create_figure(name, level)` that returns an object. Create `gruppe` with create_figure("Nova", 2) and create_figure("Orbit", 5) and print exactly Group: 2 (length of the list).
Step 2 – randomness: the class Robot is given. Create robot = Robot("Nova", random.randint(1, 5)) (`import random`) and print `1 <= robot.level <= 5` – the result must be True.
Step 3 – dictionary: the class Robot and the list `gruppe` (levels 3, 8, 5) are given. Build a dictionary `register` that maps every name to its object and print exactly Level: 8 for the entry Orbit.

Step 4 – JSON: the class Robot is given. Create Robot("Nova", 4), build the dictionary `daten` (`name`, `level`) from it and print `json.dumps(daten)`. Read the text back with `json.loads` and create a new object from it – finally print its name.
